svg.title: Monsoon Lens architecture
svg.desc: Two ECMWF forecasts are aligned to a shared run, processed by a Python pipeline into compact float16 cubes, built and deployed to GitHub Pages four times a day, and read entirely in the browser with no backend.
svg.text: IFS HRES — physics
oper/fc · 0p25 · 00z & 12z only
65 steps to T+240h · 31 MB
units: m · 3 h then 6 h after T+144h
AIFS Single — data-driven
oper/fc · 0p25 · all four cycles
41 steps to T+240h · 17 MB
units: kg m⁻² · uniform 6 h
ECMWF Open Data · CC BY 4.0
common_run — the newest cycle both models have published
pipeline/ — Python
fetch → decode → transform → encode
▪ window derived from decoded coordinates, then asserted
GRIB starts at longitude 180, so 65°E is column 980 — not 260
▪ units read per file and normalised to millimetres
AIFS/IFS accumulated tp ratio measured at 949.7 — unit, not physics
▪ de-accumulate, dividing by each interval's own length
N steps → N−1 frames; a constant divisor doubles rates after T+144h
▪ quality gates, with clamping disclosed per run
no NaNs · no negatives · plausible peak · exact byte length
peak memory < 400 MB: one global field decoded and subset at a time
Forecast cubes — float16 mm/h, [frame][lat][lon]
meta.json — grid, every frame's interval and valid time,
units, run time, stats, SHA-256, clamping diagnostics
GitHub Actions — four times a day
pytest · build cubes · verify_data.py · npm run check · vite build
two attempts per cycle, because scheduled runs are queued and ran 4.5 h late on 2026-11-12
GitHub Pages → the browser · no backend, no API, no keys
Both forecasts arrive as ~540 KB gzipped and stay in memory, so clicking a
point is an array lookup. MapLibre renders a self-contained Natural Earth
basemap; the rain field is coloured into a 141 × 141 canvas we paint ourselves,
which is also how the physics/AI swipe is done — split in data space, one texture.
